problem_severity.evidence: Plants dying is frustrating but not critical pain; mostly a learning/convenience problem; low stakes

demand_signals.evidence: r/houseplants 2.5M members; strong Instagram/TikTok plant communities; 'plant parent' trend post-pandemic

competitive_intensity.evidence: Bloomscape ($90M raised), The Sill, Horti, many subscription boxes; crowded D2C plant market

market_size.evidence: US houseplant market ~$2B; subscription segment smaller; D2C plant delivery ~$500M

execution_difficulty.evidence: Physical goods logistics complex; plant survival during shipping; AI personalization requires data

gtm_viability.evidence: Instagram/TikTok reach possible but expensive; influencer partnerships viable; high CAC for physical subscriptions

timing.evidence: Houseplant boom peaked during pandemic; still elevated but growth slowing; subscription fatigue risk

recommendation.rationale: Crowded market with well-funded competitors (Bloomscape). Physical goods logistics create execution complexity and margin pressure. AI personalization is differentiator but may not justify full subscription. Consider pivoting to: (1) software-only plant care app, (2) B2B selling to existing retailers, or (3) focusing on specific underserved niche.
next_steps: Validate AI plant care recommendations standalone (no physical goods)
Interview Bloomscape/The Sill customers about gaps and churn reasons
Explore B2B partnership with nurseries or retailers
